text:
The best climate match for the 2050s under high emissions is Walla Walla County, WA, with a good match quality, and 6 climate models agree. A lower sigma means the place's climate today is closer to the farm's future climate. 

Regarding rotations, 2 matching areas use the field's current rotation, which is a flexible mix of pulses, spring wheat, winter wheat. Other rotations used at the matching places include winter wheat to fallow, a flexible mix of fallow, pulses, winter wheat, and a flexible mix of fallow, spring wheat, winter wheat.

For hazards compared to the best match, the field has 27 days above 32c per year today compared to 37 at the match. The field has 172 frost-free days today compared to 211 at the match. For the driest month soil water percentage, the field has 18.1 percent in September today compared to 17.8 percent in September at the match.

The future climate brings changes across the seasons, with temperatures rising and precipitation amounts shifting throughout the year under high emissions. 

These findings come with candidates based on 3351 farmland cells at approximately 4 kilometers using the Cropland Data Layer.
